title: Private tenant role-sync race causing missing audit entries and transient auth drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported missing audit events and unexpected role mappings for short windows during our managed KMS envelope rotation in private clusters. The issue surfaced when the role synchronization worker raced with token reissuance after KMS rewraps, causing audit log records to be dropped and, in one customer’s case, a transient elevation for a service account. This ticket tracks the urgent patch, validation, customer communication, and follow-ups.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a private control-plane with KMS envelope rotation enabled and role-sync worker interval set to 30s
2) Create a service account and a role mapping then trigger a KMS envelope rotation for the tenant key
3) Simultaneously create short-lived impersonation tokens (simulated load) while forcing the role-sync worker to run
4) Observe missing audit entries in the control-plane audit log for the token issuance and role assignment events; in some runs the effective RBAC policy applied is stale for ~10-30s
root_cause: Race between the role-sync reconciliation path and the token reissuance path when a tenant KMS envelope rotates. The rewrap path temporarily rewrites the identity metadata with a placeholder principal while reencrypting keys; if the role-sync reconciler runs during the placeholder state it prunes role bindings and emits compacted audit entries that downstream aggregator drops due to a change in event shape. This combined behavior caused missing audit events and, under rare timing, transiently applied stale role mappings to newly minted tokens.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Hotfix: revert role-sync aggressive pruning during envelope rotations by skipping reconciles for tenants flagged as 'in-rotation' (deployed to private control planes 2026-03-01 10:30 UTC)

2) Short-term customer mitigation: instruct affected customers to avoid triggering admin role changes during scheduled KMS rotations; offered temporary manual rotation windows and schedule coordination
3) Increased audit retention and pipeline tweak: updated aggregator to accept compacted event shape for 48h window so previously dropped events can be re-ingested from control-plane buffers
rollout_plan: Canary: apply hotfix to two low-risk private clusters in staging and one customer pilot cluster (48h observation)
Gradual rollout to remaining private clusters in 6-hour batches with monitoring gates for audit event delta, role-binding churn, and token issuance latency
Force revert path if audit drop rate > 0.1% for any batch
Ship permanent fix (see postmortem_actions) in release priv-2026.03.1 after security review
test_plan: Unit tests for role-sync to skip reconcile when tenant state='in-rotation'
Integration test that simulates KMS envelope rotation under load and asserts no audit events are dropped and no stale role bindings are applied
Chaos test: randomized timing of rewrap + reconciler to verify invariants over 1,000 iterations
Manual validation with affected customers: reproduce rotation in a mirrored staging tenant and verify audit completeness
communications: Customer notifications drafted and sent to three impacted tenants with timeline, mitigation steps, and offer of joint remediation call
Post-deployment email to all private customers advising best practices for rotation windows and linking to KB: https://confluence.redwood.ai/priv-kms-rotation-guidance
postmortem_actions: 1) Implement permanent fix: decouple role-sync pruning from ephemeral identity placeholder semantics and make reconciler idempotent to placeholder transitions
2) Add explicit rotation-state to tenant metadata surfaced to all control-plane subsystems during key rewraps
3) Extend audit pipeline schema to tolerate shape changes and add strict end-to-end delivery tests
4) Update runbook: coordinate KMS envelope rotations with tenant owners and perform pre-rotation traffic quiesce when needed
5) Security review of fix and automated alerting for audit-drop anomalies
notes: Customer A (EU-finance) reported missing entries spanning 2026-02-28 17:12–17:35 UTC; audit aggregator shows 23 missing events later recovered by buffer re-ingest
Customer B (healthcare) saw a transient role elevation for a service account; we validated it did not lead to data exfil but recommended credential rotation as precaution
SRE increased control-plane buffer retention to 72h to assist potential re-ingests; will monitor storage cost impact
Security team requested embargoed timeline until patch verification completes
Follow-up scheduled: cross-team postmortem on 2026-03-10 with PM, SecOps, SRE, and representatives from affected customers
